subject: Planned: South-Central staggered I/O migration and node restarts — Aug 28 maintenance window
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Atlas Health <ops@atlashealth.com>, Novatech Analytics <infra@novatech.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Planned: South-Central staggered I/O migration and node restarts — Aug 28 maintenance window

Hi team —

We’re scheduling a targeted I/O stack migration in our south-central region (us-southcentral) on Saturday, Aug 28, to roll a new storage driver and associated kernel I/O patches. This will require staggered node restarts across host pools to apply the driver and validate I/O paths.

Planned window
- Start: 2027-08-28 02:00 UTC
- End: 2027-08-28 08:00 UTC
- Expected customer impact: brief request-level latency spikes (1–3s) during per-host cache warmup; rare transient 5–10s stalls during the host restart for affected placement groups. We expect no data loss and no customer-visible request failures beyond automatic retries.

What we’ll do
- Drain targeted host pools in small batches (3–5 hosts at a time).
- Apply the I/O driver 2.14.1 and kernel ABI shim (kmod 0.9.3).
- Run KV-cache rehydration and synthetic I/O validation per host.
- Rebalance traffic to healthy hosts during each batch.

Why this matters
- This update fixes a small class of pathological I/O stalls that have appeared under heavy multi-tenant inference workloads; it improves tail latency for long-sequence inference.

Attachments
- southcentral-io-migration-runbook.pdf (application/pdf) — runbook and rollback steps
- preflight-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet) — preflight checks for customers and internal ops

Notes for Atlas Health and Novatech
- No action required from you unless you have workloads pinned to specific host-affinity labels; if so, please reply with the label names and we’ll exclude them from the first batch.
- If you need a narrower maintenance window, let us know by EOD Monday (23 Aug) and we’ll evaluate options.

Status page and live updates will be posted to: https://status.redwood.example/incident/2027-08-28-io-migration

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai

Quick internal ops plan and confirmations before I reply to Atlas:
- Exclude labels cluster:atlas-prod and cluster:billing from batch-1 and batch-2; schedule them in batch-3 (hosts 21–30).
- Verification endpoint: /health/ingest-readonly on the customer-facing ingress (will be available between host warmup and full traffic cutover). I’ll publish the exact FQDN shortly.
- We will run a preflight at 2027-08-27T23:00Z (internal only) and share results. Priyom will own the rollback gate for each batch; Monica will own observability checks (latency tails, error spikes), Grace will coordinate customer comms and cutover notices.

Runbook summary (high level)
1) Mark hosts for drain -> 2) Sync to standby -> 3) Apply kmod & driver -> 4) Validate synthetic I/O -> 5) Rehydrate KV cache -> 6) Release host back to pool

I’ll attach the updated runbook with host assignments and batch windows to the thread.

— Priyom

Subject: Re: Planned: South-Central staggered I/O migration and node restarts — Aug 28 maintenance window

Update: maintenance complete — brief post-action summary and next steps

Status
- Window: 2027-08-28 02:05–07:58 UTC (all batches completed).
- Result: migration applied to all targeted host pools; KV-cache rehydration completed for each host after restart.
- Customer impact observed: transient tail-latency increases (~1.2–2.8s) during host warmup for ~6 minutes per host group; two short spikes (8–11s) observed for one placement group during a mis-scheduled traffic cutover — automatic retries handled the requests and no errors were returned.

What we did to mitigate the spike
- Rapid rollback candidate prepared and held (not required).
- Increased retry window and temporarily adjusted upstream load-balancer weight to accelerate draining.
- Priyom executed a targeted hotfix to the cache rehydration order for the affected placement group.

Follow-ups
- We’ll publish a concise postmortem document within 48 hours (link will be posted on the status page).
- Atlas: we excluded cluster:atlas-prod and cluster:billing from initial batches per your request and confirmed they were moved in batch-3 without customer-visible failure. Please run your ingest-readonly smoke test and let us know any anomalies.

Links and artifacts
- Completed runbook (annotated): https://drive.redwood.example/s/teams/infra/southcentral-io-migration-runbook
- Incident updates / postmortem draft: https://status.redwood.example/incident/2027-08-28-io-migration

Thanks everyone for the coordination. If you saw any ongoing anomalies, reply to this thread and we’ll prioritize a follow-up.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
